style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontColor=#232F3E;fontSize=10;fillColor=#F9FAFB;strokeColor=#6B7280;spacing=8;rounded=1;arcSize=3;" value="<b>Inside the cluster</b><br>The ingress sends each route to one service. The dashboard goes through OAuth2 Proxy (Google SSO, email allowlist) before the backend.<br>Langfuse web and worker both use RDS, Redis, ClickHouse and S3.<br>Our manifests: backend, Collector, OAuth2 Proxy, ingress. Langfuse Helm chart: Langfuse, ClickHouse, Redis.<br>Each component reads only its own secret." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="172" width="330" x="950" y="152" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="aws-igw" parent="p2" style="sketch=0;outlineConnect=0;fontColor=#232F3E;gradientColor=none;strokeColor=none;dashed=0;verticalLabelPosition=bottom;verticalAlign=top;align=center;html=1;fontSize=11;aspect=fixed;pointerEvents=1;fillColor=#8C4FFF;shape=mxgraph.aws4.internet_gateway;labelPosition=left;verticalLabelPosition=middle;align=right;verticalAlign=middle;spacingRight=6;" value="Internet gateway" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="48" width="48" x="1011" y="186" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="aws-splunk" parent="p2" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#FFFFFF;strokeColor=#232F3E;fontSize=11;fontColor=#232F3E;" value="Splunk" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="46" width="150" x="1960" y="700" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="aws-siem" parent="p2" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#FFFFFF;strokeColor=#232F3E;fontSize=11;fontColor=#232F3E;" value="SIEM" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="46" width="150" x="1960" y="770" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="aws-drnote" parent="p2" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontColor=#232F3E;fontSize=10;fillColor=#FFFBEB;strokeColor=#D97706;spacing=8;rounded=1;arcSize=3;" value="<b>HA and DR: Multi-AZ plus in-region backups (no data leaves Thailand)</b><br><b>HA:</b> two AZs. RDS Multi-AZ fails over automatically. Stateless pods run in both AZs behind one ALB. One NAT gateway per AZ.<br><b>Backups in region:</b> RDS automated backups with point-in-time recovery. AWS Backup snapshots of the ClickHouse and Redis disks. S3 versioning.<br><b>Not covered:</b> a full region outage. Recovery is a rebuild from the Kubernetes files; lost runs are sent again from GCP (a stored run never changes, and a resend is safe).<br><b>Weak point:</b> if the AZ that holds ClickHouse and Redis fails, Langfuse traces are unavailable until their disks are restored in the other AZ. Monitor grades are not affected.<br><b>To decide with the service owner:</b> recovery-time and data-loss targets, backup retention, who runs the restore drill." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="190" width="780" x="360" y="1110" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="aws-asnote" parent="p2" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontColor=#232F3E;fontSize=10;fillColor=#FFFBEB;strokeColor=#D97706;spacing=8;rounded=1;arcSize=3;" value="<b>Assumptions and items to verify</b><br>1. Not verified for ap-southeast-7: WAF, Data Firehose, IAM Identity Center, Shield Advanced, AWS Backup, RDS PostgreSQL 17.<br>2. EKS is assumed; the plan says &quot;AWS Kubernetes cluster&quot;.<br>3. Shield Standard is automatic and free. Shield Advanced is a paid subscription.<br>4. Secrets are in the Kubernetes secret store (S3-06). A managed secret service would need a plan entry.<br>5. No gateway endpoint exists for RDS. The cluster reaches RDS on a private IP. The interface endpoint is for the RDS management API; nothing in this stack calls it today.<br>6. Firehose pushes to Splunk and the SIEM; both need an HTTP endpoint that Firehose can reach.<br>7. The plan names no AWS image registry or deploy pipeline, so none is drawn. Each paid service needs a plan entry.<br>8. Plan A is drawn (RDS and S3). Plan B, if RDS and S3 are not approved by 21 October: PostgreSQL and MinIO run in the cluster.<br>9. One RDS instance holds both databases. Plan A in S3-06 has one instance for the monitor and one for Langfuse. To decide in the consultation.<br>10. Without a DNS name, Google SSO does not work, and the dashboard has only the IP allowlist (S4-01)." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="190" width="750" x="1160" y="1110" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontColor=#232F3E;fontSize=13;fillColor=#F9FAFB;strokeColor=#6B7280;spacing=8;rounded=1;arcSize=3;" value="<b>Data scope in October: identity-only</b><br>Each job sends the run identity, the counts, the status and the times (records: []), and one trace for each run. GCP spans contain no text. No customer data and no customer text reach the monitor. There is no judge and no LiteLLM call. Decided 2026-10-09; risk tier R1. Before SEND_RECORDS goes on or the judge starts, gates 3, 6 and 7 examine the change again. The monitor advises people. Langfuse web and worker 4.50.0, Helm chart 2.1.3 · OTel Collector contrib 0.161.0 · ClickHouse 25.12.11.4 · Redis 7.4.11 · OAuth2 Proxy v7.15.5 · backend on python:3.12-slim" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="95" width="1055" x="20" y="1540" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="transition" parent="1" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontColor=#232F3E;fontSize=13;fillColor=#F9FAFB;strokeColor=#6B7280;spacing=8;rounded=1;arcSize=3;" value="<b>From phase 1 to phase 2 (S4-01, S4-02)</b><br>Each job changes three settings: the API URL, the OTLP endpoint and the API key (a new production key). The path changes from the private VPC to the internet through Cloud NAT, and AWS allows only those egress IPs. HTTPS, the DNS name and the dashboard SSO start with phase 2.<br>Hard stops: no production install before gate 6 says Yes. No production runs before gate 7 says Yes. The test host stays for one week as the fallback." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="95" width="1055" x="1095" y="1540" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div:
Inside the cluster
The ingress sends each route to one service. The dashboard goes through OAuth2 Proxy (Google SSO, email allowlist) before the backend.
Langfuse web and worker both use RDS, Redis, ClickHouse and S3.
Our manifests: backend, Collector, OAuth2 Proxy, ingress. Langfuse Helm chart: Langfuse, ClickHouse, Redis.
Each component reads only its own secret.

div.div:
HA and DR: Multi-AZ plus in-region backups (no data leaves Thailand)
HA: two AZs. RDS Multi-AZ fails over automatically. Stateless pods run in both AZs behind one ALB. One NAT gateway per AZ.
Backups in region: RDS automated backups with point-in-time recovery. AWS Backup snapshots of the ClickHouse and Redis disks. S3 versioning.
Not covered: a full region outage. Recovery is a rebuild from the Kubernetes files; lost runs are sent again from GCP (a stored run never changes, and a resend is safe).
Weak point: if the AZ that holds ClickHouse and Redis fails, Langfuse traces are unavailable until their disks are restored in the other AZ. Monitor grades are not affected.
To decide with the service owner: recovery-time and data-loss targets, backup retention, who runs the restore drill.

switch.text: HA and DR: Multi-AZ plus in-region backups (no data leaves Thailand)...

div.div:
Assumptions and items to verify
1. Not verified for ap-southeast-7: WAF, Data Firehose, IAM Identity Center, Shield Advanced, AWS Backup, RDS PostgreSQL 17.
2. EKS is assumed; the plan says "AWS Kubernetes cluster".
3. Shield Standard is automatic and free. Shield Advanced is a paid subscription.
4. Secrets are in the Kubernetes secret store (S3-06). A managed secret service would need a plan entry.
5. No gateway endpoint exists for RDS. The cluster reaches RDS on a private IP. The interface endpoint is for the RDS management API; nothing in this stack calls it today.
6. Firehose pushes to Splunk and the SIEM; both need an HTTP endpoint that Firehose can reach.
7. The plan names no AWS image registry or deploy pipeline, so none is drawn. Each paid service needs a plan entry.
8. Plan A is drawn (RDS and S3). Plan B, if RDS and S3 are not approved by 21 October: PostgreSQL and MinIO run in the cluster.
9. One RDS instance holds both databases. Plan A in S3-06 has one instance for the monitor and one for Langfuse. To decide in the consultation.
10. Without a DNS name, Google SSO does not work, and the dashboard has only the IP allowlist (S4-01).

div.div:
Data scope in October: identity-only
Each job sends the run identity, the counts, the status and the times (records: []), and one trace for each run. GCP spans contain no text. No customer data and no customer text reach the monitor. There is no judge and no LiteLLM call. Decided 2026-10-09; risk tier R1. Before SEND_RECORDS goes on or the judge starts, gates 3, 6 and 7 examine the change again. The monitor advises people. It never changes or stops a model or a job.

div.div:
From phase 1 to phase 2 (S4-01, S4-02)
Each job changes three settings: the API URL, the OTLP endpoint and the API key (a new production key). The path changes from the private VPC to the internet through Cloud NAT, and AWS allows only those egress IPs. HTTPS, the DNS name and the dashboard SSO start with phase 2.
Hard stops: no production install before gate 6 says Yes. No production runs before gate 7 says Yes. The test host stays for one week as the fallback.
